summary_html: A **court reverses or vacates** a CPS or agency decision due to procedural error, insufficient evidence, or constitutional violation. Federal review data (CFSR, ASFA) tracks judicial determinations on reasonable efforts and due process.
authority_html:
- **Adoption and Safe Families Act (ASFA)** — judicial findings of 'reasonable efforts' compliance  
- **CFSR Regulations (45 CFR Part 1355)** — federal review of judicial/agency conformity  
- **42 U.S.C. § 1983** — civil-rights remedy for unconstitutional removals (14th & 4th Amendments).

provisions_triggered.name: Due Process / Law of the Land

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The Court reversed, holding the juvenile court violated the father's due-process right to notice and an opportunity to be heard in the early stages of the case, and that 'other aggravating circumstances' relieving the Department of reasonable efforts under Wyo. Stat. Ann. § 14-2-309(c)(v) must be as severe as the enumerated grounds.
key_cases.relevance: A working example of appellate reversal of a juvenile-court order for procedural due-process error.
key_cases.quote: the legislature logically meant for “other aggravating circumstances” to meet the same level of severity as set out in the preceding provisions

key_cases.case_name: Matter of Termination of Parental Rights to RVR, KAR and RLR
key_cases.holding: The Court held that Wyo. Stat. Ann. § 14-2-318(a) creates neither a mandatory right to counsel nor a statutory right to effective assistance of counsel in termination proceedings, and affirmed the refusal to set aside an entry of default against the father.
key_cases.relevance: Forecloses ineffective-assistance-of-counsel as a statutory ground for appellate reversal of a Wyoming termination order and sets the good-cause standard for setting aside default.
key_cases.quote: Wyoming Statute § 14-2-318(a) does not create a statutory right to counsel or a statutory right to effective assistance of counsel in termination of parental rights cases

key_cases.case_name: BSC v. Natrona County Department of Family Services
key_cases.holding: Applying Lassiter and the Mathews v. Eldridge factors case by case, the Court held the district court did not deny the incarcerated, indigent father due process when it refused to appoint counsel for him at the hearing terminating his parental rights.
key_cases.relevance: Defines the narrow circumstances in which denial of appointed counsel at a Wyoming termination hearing is reversible due-process error.
key_cases.quote: we conclude that BSC's due process rights were not violated when the district court refused to appoint counsel to represent him at the termination proceeding

key_cases.case_name: In the Interest of JW v. State
key_cases.holding: The Court reversed a permanency order placing children with non-relative foster parents and remanded with instructions to place them with their uncle and aunt, rejecting the argument that the federal and state kinship-placement preferences are merely precatory.
key_cases.relevance: A rare appellate reversal of an agency-driven permanency placement for failure to honor the kinship preference.
key_cases.quote: We are unable to accept these characterizations given the high stakes in play here

key_cases.case_name: Matter of Termination of Parental Rights to JJD
key_cases.holding: Reviewing for plain error, the Court held the mother was not denied a meaningful opportunity to be heard when the district court proceeded with the termination hearing and allowed her to appear and testify by telephone while her counsel appeared in person.
key_cases.relevance: Defines when a procedural irregularity at a termination hearing is and is not reversible plain error on appeal.
key_cases.quote: The district court did not deny Mother a meaningful opportunity to be heard when it proceeded with the termination hearing and allowed her to appear by phone

key_cases.case_name: In re Termination of Parental Rights to TJH (Herden v. State ex rel. Department of Family Services)
key_cases.holding: Applying the Mathews v. Eldridge factors, the Court affirmed the termination, holding the defaulted mother's due-process rights were not violated when the district court held the evidentiary default hearing by video conference and limited her participation to cross-examination and argument rather than permitting her to present her own best-interests evidence.
key_cases.relevance: This is Wyoming's companion due-process authority to ECH and JJD on a parent's meaningful opportunity to be heard, and it fixes how far a court may limit a defaulted parent's participation before the order becomes reversible.
key_cases.quote: Balancing the Mathews factors, it is clear Mother received adequate process under the circumstances of this case even though she was not permitted to present evidence on Child's best interests

state_agency.name: Wyoming Department of Family Services
state_agency.hotline: No statewide hotline. Call the DFS field office in the county where the child lives — the list is at dfs.wyo.gov/about/contact-us

timeline_requirements.starts_from: Entry of the appealable juvenile court order, judgment or decree (Wyo. Stat. § 14-3-432(a) applies the Wyoming Rules of Appellate Procedure; W.R.A.P. 2.01(a) sets the 30 days)
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Timely filing of a notice of appeal is jurisdictional (W.R.A.P. 1.03(a))
